answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The crystal is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the relic. What survives to the zephyr is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, forfeited on duplicate submission, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name.
